what: aggregation of stored-weight int8-vs-bf16 error by block and by module kind; no new measurement
is_not: Sol's kernel INT8. See this file's docstring -- analyze_sol_error.py's quant_l2 is a different quantity and the two were crossed once.
findings: Stored-weight INT8 error is FLAT across blocks: 1.086x from best to worst over all 50. Block 49 ranks 6/50. The worst blocks are [2, 1, 0, 3, 5], the shallow end, not the deep end. So block 49's Sol-kernel behaviour has no counterpart in its weights, and re-baking the checkpoint cannot address it.
attn.out_proj is the worst module kind under INT8 at 1.18x qkv_proj on the mean, and worse in the tail: row_rel p95 0.01281 against 0.01008, row_rel max 0.03710 against 0.01509.

Under fp8_scaled all four kinds are equal to four decimal places, so out_proj's excess is a property of the INT8 SCHEME rather than of the out_proj weights. That is what makes it a candidate for different treatment in a re-bake; it is also the only lane here the bf16 release is needed for.
not_measured: whether out_proj's excess reaches the output. This is stored-weight fidelity only -- the same caveat the source record carries.
why the INT8 scheme treats out_proj worse. Outlier structure the rotation does not spread is the obvious candidate and is untested.
any block-49 activation property. Nothing here looks at activations.
weight_only_caveat_2026-08-31: Added 2026-08-31. int8_convrot is W8A8: `comfy_kitchen`'s `int8_linear` rotates the activation online with the same Hadamard and quantises it PER TOKEN before an int8 GEMM whose accumulation is exact (docs/research/comfyui_h3_t2va_trace.md sections 1.7-1.8: 'all the error is in the two roundings'). Every number in this file is a stored-WEIGHT distance and is blind to the activation rounding by construction. It therefore cannot rank module kinds by what they cost at run time, and a flat result for a knob whose job is to spread outliers is not evidence the knob is inert. The runtime decomposition is docs/open_experiments.md #23. This field records a caveat that was always true of the measurement and was dropped by prose citing it.
